articleTitle: Upgrade Perturbation and Observation of MPPT Strategy via Fuzzy Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel intelligent algorithm based on the fast Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) is proposed to evaluate the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) founded on the Perturbation and Observation method P&O. Several techniques of solar energy controller have been proposed in the literature, among them the Perturbation and Observation method, fixed and variable incremental conductance methods, and Fractional open circuit voltage. Many drawbacks disadvantage the P&O technique, In a steady state, significant oscillations are centered on the MPP, which in turn to a waste of available energy as well, and rapid changes in atmospheric conditions cause a notable deviation in the MPP. In addition, the complex implementation of P&O. To avoid all defects mentioned above, a novel MPPT algorithm built on the FLC is proposed. Error and derived error (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E\& {{\Delta }}E$</tex>) between the reference input and actual input represent the inputs data of FLC, while the duty cycle (D) is the target data. The main aim of this work is to overcome the major defects of the traditional P&O method via the FLC controller. The simulation andexperimental validation tests prove the effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency of the FLC algorithm and support the system's analysis.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Perturb and Observe Incremental Conductance and Particle Swarm Optimisation for Maximum Power Point Tracking Under Changing Irradiance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Increasing the power output of photovoltaic (PV) systems is critical for efficient energy harvesting. This work gives a comprehensive comparison of three frequently used Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithms: Perturb and Observe (P&O), Incremental Conductance (Inc-Cond), and Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO). The research looks at the performance of these algorithms under constant and variable irradiance settings with a constant temperature. The simulation findings highlight the merits and weaknesses of each method in terms of tracking efficiency, convergence speed, and robustness. The findings provide useful insights for determining the best MPPT algorithm for PV systems depending on unique environmental circumstances.

articleTitle: Improve Lifespan of Battery Energy Storage in Remote Area Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The costly nature of battery storage is one of the barriers to using solar energy in remote area power system (RAPS). Due to the continuous high current that is used from the battery as a consequence of the nature of operation in (RAPS) applications, batteries often need to be changed more frequently than hybrid energy storage devices. The system's total life-cycle cost (LCC) will rise as a consequence of this. In this study, an independent photovoltaic (PV) and battery system for a RAPS application are analyzed, and it suggests that supercapacitors (SCs) be employed in order to rise the lifespan of the batteries and minimize the total cost to operate throughout the system. The Photovoltaics and battery storage solely (also known as without SC) and the Photovoltaics, battery, and SC (also known as with SC) scenarios are both established. Furthermore, energy management technique is used to unsure, balance power among the solar energy, storage devices, and load. Also, to regulate DC link voltage. The efficacy of the suggested system is examined by employing MATLAB/Simulink under a multitude of conditions including demand load and irradiation fluctuations.

articleTitle: Intelligent Techniques Employing LSTM and ANFIS Models for Fault Detection and Isolation in a Wind Turbine Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: With the increasing reliance on wind energy as a renewable power source and the expanding deployment of wind farms, a multitude of technical challenges arise, necessitating the implementation of effective maintenance strategies to ensure optimal performance and reliable operation. Through the execution of regular inspections, proactive repairs, and condition-based monitoring, wind farm operators can identify potential issues and address them before they lead to costly breakdowns or significant energy production losses. In this regard, preventive maintenance has emerged as a proactive approach aimed at identifying and rectifying potential issues before they escalate into costly failures or downtime. This paper provides an overview of the application of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in preventive maintenance for wind turbines. LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) algorithms are used, relying on historical and real-time data to identify patterns, detect anomalies, and predict potential failures, enabling proactive maintenance actions. Additionally, an ANFIS (Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System) approach is employed for fault classification. The results obtained demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed model. (

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Cost-Effective IoT-Enabled Multi-Parameter System for Water Quality Monitoring in Aquaculture and Aquaponics
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper details a cost-effective IoT-based system that monitors water quality in aquaculture and aquaponics. The system uses low-cost probes equipped with a conditioning module to measure pH, conductivity, total dissolved solids (TDS), turbidity, and temperature. Automatic temperature compensation is incorporated for pH and TDS measurements. The data processing and communication are performed using an ESP8266 NodeMCU, which connects to a Firebase database through a Wi-Fi connection. The collected data can be accessed by network users via an IP address, enabling real-time monitoring. The system features an OLED screen for parameter visualization, an ADS1115 ADC for accurate sensor measurements, and a 3D-printed case for housing the components. The system also includes automatic calibration functionality using standard calibration solutions. This paper demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of an affordable solution for continuous water quality monitoring in aquaculture and aquaponics systems and provides metrology for proper sensor integration and calibration.

articleTitle: Real-Time Implementation of the Luenberger Torque Observer for an Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Currently, the technology of high-performance variable speed drives without mechanical sensors is widely used in the industrial environment. This preference arises from the exorbitant costs and fragility associated with mechanical sensors. This investigation aims to establish, implement, and empirically validate a Luenberger Observer for wheel torque within an electric propulsion framework that employs induction motors. The proposed observer structure focuses on the complete dynamic model of an induction motor. Concerning the rotor fluxes, they are estimated using the electrical model. On the other hand, the torque is observed using the mechanical model. A real-time implementation was performed on a DSpace 1104 board designed for a 1.5 kW induction motor to verify the proposed observer's effectiveness. The experiment results show that the proposed method exhibits satisfactory performance, affirming its effectiveness and robustness and giving valuable insights into its practical applicability.

articleTitle: Silica Nanofiber-Based Evanescent Optical Kerr Effect in Nonlinear Liquid Media
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Tapered optical fibers with ultra-small radii provide an intriguing platform for confining light, leading to the generation of nonlinear effects and the formation of an intense evanescent field that effectively interacts with the surrounding medium. In this paper, we give a theoretical demonstration of the evanescent field's major contribution to the Kerr effect observed in a silica nanofiber surrounded by liquids at a wavelength of 780 nm, including water, ethanol, and acetone. Our findings reveal an evanescent Kerr effect that outperforms the traditional Kerr effect within the nanofiber core when the nanofiber diameter is less than 0.793 particularly in the presence of acetone. As a result, these nanofibers exhibit exceptional promise as sensors for scrutinizing external media, particularly in hard-to-reach locations, by harnessing the potential of the evanescent optical Kerr effect.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis via Kalman Filters and ANFIS Classifiers for a Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The operation mode of wind turbines becomes more challenging because they are exposed to environmental factors and operating conditions for extended periods. Optimizing their availability involves preventing faults effectively and early to avoid production losses. To preserve this critical power source, a fault detection and isolation strategy must be planned to manage all potential faults. Sensors, system components, and actuators of wind turbines are susceptible to various types of faults. This paper aims to propose an efficient fault detection and isolation system based on artificial intelligence techniques, such as ANFIS models and Kalman observers, for the wind turbine machine. An equivalent model is elaborated for residual generation and fault diagnosis in horizontal axis wind turbine parts. The proposed structure can generate effective residuals following the occurrence of faults and determine their type and location. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed fault detection and isolation strategy for wind turbine machines.

articleTitle: Design of low Profile, High Bandwidth Circular Patch Antenna at 28 GHz for Fifth Generation Wireless Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This article introduces a novel technique to develop a circular patch antenna specifically tailored for 5G wireless technology operating in the 28 GHz frequency range. By thought-fully incorporating a rectangular slot into the design on a Rogers substrate, not only does the antenna's performance get enhanced, but its bandwidth also gets expanded. This expansion in bandwidth allows the antenna to effectively cover a broader frequency range, which holds immense significance for practical applications. The compact design occupies only 8.3×8.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of space. Through simulations and measurements, it is demonstrated that the antenna achieves a 10 dB higher gain, ensuring a significant improvement in signal power. It delivers a bandwidth of 2.23 GHz, extending across the spectrum from 27.77 GHz to 30 GHz. The resonance analysis reveals a good return loss of -34.3 dB, indicating excellent signal matching. Furthermore, the antenna achieves a voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of 1.11, facilitating the effective transfer of radio frequency energy. The results indicate satisfactory performance in terms of matching, losses, and efficiency, positioning this design as a promising candidate for efficient communication in 5G networks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Transport Systems Using High Altitude Platform Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The rapid development of technology in recent years has brought about significant advances in the field of Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). In order to enhance the sustainability, efficiency, and safety of transportation applications, this article highlights the importance of using High Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS) as a crucial communication solution. This detailed exploration aims to illustrate the enhanced capabilities of connected HAPS and demonstrate how they exceed those of conventional satellite systems. In addition, the article also delves into the actual performance of HAPS through a comprehensive analysis of factors such as surface cover, atmospheric attenuation and data rate. To illustrate the practical implementation of HAPS in ITS as a solution, a case study of the highway of the Hauts Plateaux in Algeria is provided.

articleTitle: Analysis and Experimental Implementation of SHEPWM based on Newton-Raphson Algorithm on Three-Phase Inverter using Dspace 1104
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper discusses the analysis, simulation and experimental investigation of selective harmonics elimination with pulse width modulation using Newton-Raphson algorithm for three phase inverter. The purpose of using this modulation strategy is to increase the life span of the switching elements and improve the inverter output voltage. This study offers a general analytical description of the harmonic problem and explains the application of a Newton-Raphson algorithm for eliminating some target harmonics step by step. The accuracy of the method has been confirmed using MATLAB environment with a digital signal processor that goes by the name of Dspace 1104. The experimental results matches the simulation ones perfectly, thereby strengthening the previous studies about the effectiveness of the selective harmonics elimination based on Newton-Raphson algorithm.

articleTitle: Real-Time People Counting System using YOLOv8 Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive real-time people counting system that utilizes the advanced YOLOv8 object detection algorithm. The proposed method aims to accurately track individuals within a video stream and provide precise counts of people entering and exiting specific areas of interest. The system combines state-of-the-art computer vision techniques, leveraging the robust object detection capabilities of YOLOv8, along with efficient tracking mechanisms and region-based analysis. The system demonstrates exceptional accuracy and robustness in people-counting tasks through extensive experimental evaluations conducted across various scenarios. The results highlight the system's effectiveness in crowd management, occupancy analysis, and surveillance applications.

articleTitle: Improvement of the MCKD Process using EMD and Feature Mode Decomposition under Bearing Damage in Induction Motors: Comparison Study
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Effective detection of bearing faults in induction motors is crucial for ensuring optimal performance and preventing costly breakdowns in industrial systems. This paper presents a comparative study between two prominent techniques, namely Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) integrated with the Maximum Correlated Kurtosis Deconvolution (MCKD) and Feature Mode Decomposition (FMD) For the diagnosis of bearing defects in induction motors (IMs). To evaluate the effectiveness of both techniques, a comprehensive set of experiments is conducted using experimental data. This data contains various bearing fault scenarios (healthy or faulty induction motors). The results demonstrate the capabilities of EMD-MCKD and FMD-MCKD techniques in detecting different types of bearing faults, such as inner ring, outer ring, and ball faults. Furthermore, the comparative analysis considers several performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and computational complexity. This work contribution lies in providing researchers and practitioners with valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of EMD-MCKD and FMD-MCKD techniques for bearing fault detection in induction motors. This paper contributes to the field of monitoring the state and detecting faults in rotating machinery. These developed techniques try to ensure the accurate and the reliability to detect bearing faults in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Forecasting using AI techniques and LSTM Deep Learning Network in Southern West of Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The accurate forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) power refers to the ability to predict the amount of electrical energy that will be generated by a photovoltaic system in response to given irradiation and temperature. This forecast is important for several reasons, including optimizing the system's performance, facilitating energy trade and managing network integration. In this article, Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural network are used for forecasting the output power of a photovoltaic power generation station using a set of historical time series data composed of photovoltaic power, irradiation and temperature. The data has been collected by the measuring environmental variables and generated power every 15 minutes from a station located in the city of Adrar in the Southern West of Algeria. The accuracy of the LSTM based model is compared to other classic models such as ANFIS and ANN for the same conditions. The results of the trained LSTM model show a slight difference between the forecasted and measured power with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) value equal to MAE= 127.10. The training and evaluation of the PV power forecasts by other techniques give an average accuracy MAE= 1.3857 for the ANN model, and MAE=3.0052*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> for the ANFIS model.

articleTitle: Radio Channel Predicted Model of Deployed Cellular Network in Algiers City
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The study of the radio environment characteristics is necessary to enhance the precision of the cellular network mobile station localization. In this work, we use a linear regression technique based on the ordinary least squares approach to illustrate a radio channel model customized for the cellular network radio environment of Algiers, Algeria. We use the Log-normal, K-factor, and Okumura-Hata models. Real RSSI measurements were made on a deployed cellular network with the aid of special software made for this purpose. The generated findings can be verified by computing the square root of the mean square error between the real data, the radio measurements, and the predicted data created from the used model. The new model could improve the efficiency of the cellular network radio systems deployed in Algiers.

articleTitle: Renewable Photovoltaic/Wind system with battery storage for water pumping in a small-scale area
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The paper provides simulation and experimental study of a hybrid renewable system (photovoltaic/wind turbine) with battery storage. A design method is used to calculate the photovoltaic and the wind generators number. An application for the water pumping was done for the irradiance, temperature and wind speed profile of a day measured in the Bejaia area. The overall hybrid pumping system with batteries was then investigated by an experimental study, where tests were made under various total dynamic heads (TDH) to show the different performances regarding the flow rate and the pump efficiency variations of the proposed system. A comparison between the different results is presented, concluding that the studied system would be feasible for water pumping purposes on a small scale in the region of Bejaia (Algeria).

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection Using Circularly Polarized Printed UWB Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper introduces a breast model system that utilizes a circularly polarized printed ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna for the detection of breast tumors. The antenna, with dimensions of 30 mm × 25 mm × 1.5 mm, offers a wide UWB capability of 115.79% within the frequency range of 4 GHz to 15 GHz, complying with the requirements of The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) band. Additionally, the proposed antenna exhibits a broad axial ratio bandwidth spanning from 4.56 GHz to 7.11 GHz (43.7%). It showcases favorable characteristics, including a maximum gain of 4.5 dBi, approximate radiation efficiency of 85 % within the operating bandwidth, and consistent radiation patterns. The antenna is integrated into a specifically designed system model that incorporates the electromagnetic properties of a human breast, enabling the detection of abnormal objects. Detailed investigations are conducted to analyze the impact of tumor size on the antenna's reflection responses, aiming to enhance tumor detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Power Transmission Line Fault Diagnosis Using Discrete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In this paper, a new method for detecting short-circuit faults on transmission lines using discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is proposed. This work presents a single-ended based technique where the three-phase current data on bus 1 is measured and decomposed to level 6 by DWT and then the detail coefficients are calculated which are also compared with thresholds to detect faults and classify faults. In order to verify the proposed ideas, various short-circuit fault simulations are performed on 230 kV, 50 Hz, and 100 km transmission lines in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. The performance of the proposed method is analyzed through various case studies with different fault locations and fault types, and the simulation results prove the efficiency of the proposed algorithm

articleTitle: Identification of PV Module Parameters Considering Output Power
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The identification of the parameters of a photovoltaic module based on the experimental output characteristics (current-voltage-power) is an essential step for the simulation, optimization and control of photovoltaic systems. This research work presents a method to extract the optimal parameters of PV module. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed technique we used experimental data, these data contain different I-V curves and they were obtained in outdoor conditions. The simulation results are compared with the experimental data of the PV cell. Finally, the estimated parameters are applied to predict the energy produced by the photovoltaic panel, which were then compared to the energy obtained from the actual data of the photovoltaic system.

articleTitle: Multichannel 1D-CNN and Hilbert Transform Based Bearing Fault Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Bearings rank among the most vital components of rotary machines, approximately 30% of total defects leading to machine breakdown are attributed to their failure, making it one of the most prevalent issues in machinery equipment that results in severe damage. Therefore, bearing faults detection and diagnosis has been a heated research topic. Recently, the utilization of deep learning algorithms has become widespread in the field of machine health monitoring. Convolutional neural network (CNN) has been extensively studied and applied recently in this paper a one-dimensional CNN (1D-CNN) based Hilbert transform is proposed in order to explore the effect using of the envelope spectrum with the Multichannel input CNN. For the purpose of evaluating the performance of the proposed approach using the accuracy and loss function rate are analyzed, the suggested approach has demonstrated a notable level of classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Algerian Potential of Biodiesel Production from Vegetable Oils: Jatropha Curcas and Olive Pomace Feedstocks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In light of the economic crisis in the world now, the increasing demand for fossil fuels has become harmful to the environment, so it is necessary to find more effective alternative fuels with less harmful effects on the environment. Biodiesel is a fuel that may be produced from the organic wastes of edible, non-edible, microbial, and waste oils. In this paper, we study using two different feedstocks for producing biodiesel, Jatropha Curcas L. and olive pomace. In particular, we discuss the feasibility, availability, and capacity of sustainable biodiesel production in Algeria. Regarding the use of Jatropha Curcas L. as a feedstock, we show that Algeria has great potential, suitable climate, large uncultivated lands, and unexploited treated and untreated wastewater. All of these conditions are ideal to cultivate Jatropha Curcas L. and produce biodiesel with good quality and properties. We found that if Algeria cultivates the same area as Indonesia, China, Brazil, or Tanzania, then 2.3%, 2.7%, 0.27%, or 0.23% of half of the total annual diesel consumption will be produced. The other feedstock studied in this paper is olive pomaces resulting from the production of olive oil. Algeria is one of the Mediterranean countries with a significant production of olive oil. We show that the 2022 estimated waste from this industry, approximately 162.000 tons of olive pomace, will produce 0.24% of the total annual diesel consumption in Algeria.

articleTitle: MPPT based FPA Control for PV Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Shading of a photovoltaic module has dramatic consequences on its power-voltage curve and even if a part of a module or cell is shaded, a significant decrease in the power produced is then the consequence. This partial shading may be due to chimneys, trees or other building parts. This work proposes a metaheuristic algorithm to find the maximum power point of photovoltaic systems under partial shading. This work discusses and presents, in first section, a Flower pollination algorithm applied to control MPPT of PV connected to DC load, to show the feasibility of the proposed technique, we will compare it with Whale Optimization algorithm. In the second section, the proposed technique will be used in pumping system as AC Load (induction motor as load controlled by direct torque control via inverter and connected to a centrifugal pump), to control MPPT of PV panels and also to control the DC link voltage.

articleTitle: Routing Protocols in VANET, Study and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET) is a significant area of research in data applications. Its primary goal is to enhance traffic efficiency and address various challenges while offering improved services to customers. One notable advantage of VANET is its potential to alleviate traffic congestion and enhance road safety by minimizing accidents. However, as with any wireless network lacking infrastructure, the routing task becomes particularly challenging, particularly when dealing with mobile nodes. The mobility of vehicles in VANET leads to rapid changes in network topology, resulting in intermittent connections between source and destination nodes. This paper aims to assess the performance of different routing protocols by analyzing them and proposing various VANET routing protocol scenarios. The simulations conducted using NS3 simulator and SUMO demonstrate the significant impact of routing protocols on VANET network performance.

articleTitle: Blind Cyclostationary Spectrum Sensing Technique Algorithm for Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Cyclostationary Spectrum Sensing (CSS) techniques are commonly used to detect primary users in Cognitive Radio (CR) networks by exploiting the cyclostationary nature of many wireless signals. CSS techniques have demonstrated impressive results in detecting primary users in CR networks, particularly in situations with low signal-to-noise ratios and multi-user interference. Nonetheless, CSS still faces challenges in handling signal variations and implementing high-complexity systems, which are active areas of research. The premise of this paper is that noise is generally a signal that lacks correlation. The paper suggests that if the input signal has a periodicity, the autocorrelation function can enhance this periodicity, while if the input signal is non-periodic, it can create a structure that lacks periodicity. The suggested approach involves utilizing the outcome of the autocorrelation module as an input for a new blind cyclostationary spectrum detection technique. This paper involves introducing the optimized detector parameters and evaluating its performance in simulation environments. Moreover, the simulation results presented in the paper demonstrate a 2.5 dB improvement in detection performance compared to the conventional cyclostationary technique. This indicates the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing the accuracy of detecting primary users in CR networks.

articleTitle: Design and Tuning of Fuzzy Controller using Human Inspired Algorithm for Speed Control of PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: designing a decent controller for a speed control of an alternative current (AC) machine, such as the PMSM can be very challenging, the conventional PID and PI controllers are the most used in the industry, but they lack the robustness and the rapid response of A fuzzy controller(FC), the fuzzy controller however needs a very precise scaling of its inputs, outputs, and its membership functions (MFS), this could be done with some serious user experience, or via trial and error technique, which is very time consuming and inconsistent, in this paper a human inspired optimization algorithm called Sewing Training-Based Optimization (STBO) was used to tune the parameters of a specially designed FC, within an hour of tuning the obtained FC managed to achieve significantly better speed tracking, and produce way less current harmonics than the conventional PID and PI controllers.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Non-Linear Observer-Based State Feedback Controller for Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This research focuses on the quadratic stabilization of an induction motor, conceptualized as a polytopic blend, assuring H-infinity tracking performance. Initially, the nonlinear model of the induction motor in the synchronous reference frame is transformed into a Takagi-Sugeno model with non-measurable decision variables using a sector non-linearity transformation. Following that, the Mean Value Theorem is applied to design a nonlinear observer-based state feedback controller. Utilizing the second Lyapunov theorem, convergence conditions are expressed in a Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) format. The observer and controller gains are derived by solving a combination of LMI constraints in a singular step using the MATLAB/YALMIP toolbox. The proposed method's effectiveness and performance are confirmed through experimental validation.

articleTitle: Design and Sizing of Wind Blades Based on Generator Parameters for Small Wind Turbines for Low Wind Regions
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Renewable energy sources, particularly wind energy, have gained significant traction in recent years as a sustainable and eco-friendly alternative to conventional power generation. Among various wind energy technologies, small wind turbines have emerged as promising solutions for decentralized energy production, catering to localized power demands. However, designing an efficient and reliable small wind turbine necessitates a deep understanding of key technical aspects, innovative approaches, and lessons learned from previous research efforts. In this research paper presents a method to determine the blades shape that ensure the rated power of 3KW and 5KW small wind turbine installed in north of Algeria.in which the mean wind speed equals 3m/s at 10m of high. The method based on the generator rate data as rotation speed (250rpm) and deferent rated wind speed values (10m/s,11m/s and 12m/s). In this case, the investigation analysis has been done by using Qblade software. The results demonstrated that the models designed at 10m/s present the best models with high annual energy production but, it should equip by gear system with conversation ration equals 1.62 for the both small wind turbine (3KW and 5KW).

articleTitle: All Optical 2R Regeneration Based on Optical Parabolic Pulses for High-Bit-Rate Links
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The primary objective of this study is to develop an All-optical 2R regenerator (Reamplification and Reshaping) that integrates optical parabolic pulses. The key goal is to enhance transmission performance by decreasing noise and improving the quality of transmitted signals through the utilization of generated similaritons in Raman amplifier fiber. The results confirm that the proposed 2R regenerator was efficient to regenerate signals with high data rate ranging from 40 Gb/s to 160 Gb/s. The performance of this regenerator is evaluated via the quality factor (Q) and the eye diagram of the received signals.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of P&O and P&O-PI MPPT Using RT-Lab Under Real Atmospheric Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to see the behavior of a stand-alone photovoltaic system in real time using the RT-Lab. In order to increase the power extracted from the solar panel, it is necessary to operate the photovoltaic (PV) system at the maximum power point (MPP). Also, this paper presents a comparative study, through experimental work, between the perturb and observe (P&O) and P&O based on PI algorithms, under different real atmospheric conditions. However, this study was divided into two parts; the first represents a brief introduction of the characteristics of the photovoltaic panel “GALIX” “JW-G2100” model and the last part mainly concerns the configuration and implementation of the proposed model using RT-Lab “OP-5700” in order to analyze the different results obtained from different control methods of maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Experimental results of the photovoltaic system, which was constructed at the Electrotechnical Laboratory of the National Polytechnic School of Constantine, will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Deep Learning Approach for Alzheimer Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Numerous studies have explored the potential of deep learning (DL) in the early diagnosis of Alzheimer disease (AD). DL models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated their potential in accurately detecting and classifying AD based on various data sources, including brain imaging scans and clinical data. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a brain imaging tool that helps in AD detecting at an early stage and this can help to slow its progression. In this study, we developed and compared two CNN models from scratch for the classification of AD stages. The first model consisted of four convolutional layers, while the second model used five convolutional layers. By examining the results of both models, we aimed to identify the impact of the depth of the CNN architecture on the classification performance. To address the issue of imbalanced datasets, we employed data augmentation techniques. The results of our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed models with accuracies of the models of 94.79 and 98.30 respectively. Additionally, we conducted a comprehensive comparison between our approaches and state-of-the-art models in the literature that have been used to classify the same dataset. We evaluated the models using various performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F-measure.

articleTitle: Improved ASR System based on CNN-LSTM Acoustic Model for Mobile Voice
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The increasing demand for data communication is not only limited to wired connections but has also spread to the wireless world. People now desire access to information while on the move, and this has become possible with the deployment of advanced technologies. Furthermore, mobile devices with improved speech input interfaces provide users with easy access to these data services. In automatic mobile speech recognition systems, the variability caused by the environment (presence of noise) leads to different types of disparities between observations and acoustic models, which generates low recognition rates in noisy conditions. The present work aims to improve the performance of the automatic speech recognition system “ASR” by using more robust acoustic parameters such as Mel spectrogram features, Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients “MFCC”, Power Normalized Cepstral Coefficients “PNCC”, Gammatone Cepstral coefficients “GTCC” and the robust MFCC extracted from the “ETSI-AFE” standard “The European Telecommunications Standards Institute advanced frontend”. This parameter “AFE-MFCC” based on speech enhancement yields higher recognition rates in noisy environments. To demonstrate the robustness and strength of this parameter, we integrated a robust acoustic model resulting from the concatenation of two neuronal models, the convolutional neural network “CNN” and the Long Short-Term Memory “LSTM” network. This combined system “CNN-LSTM” based on the “AFE-MFCC” parameter leads to better recognition rates in low signal-to-noise ratio “SNR” environments.

articleTitle: An Efficient Extraction of the Bias Dependent Extrinsic Resistances of the HEMT GaN/SiC
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: A small-signal modelling of the HEMT GaN transistor at high frequency requires a precise extraction of all the values of the small-signal equivalent circuit elements. In this paper, we focus on the extraction of the bias extrinsic resistances of HEMT GaN /SiC transistor by using the linear regression techniques on parametric curves defined by the real parts of the transistor Z-matrix at different bias points, i.e. set the gate voltage to a fixed value, while varying the drain-source voltage over a range of values. This allows to capture the device behavior under different bias conditions. We propose an approach for the extraction of the bias extrinsic resistances and describe the whole extraction procedure, discuss the new results and giving some concluding remarks.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Various Multicarrier Modulation Formats for 5G Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The existing generation of mobile networks is facing challenges to satisfy the growing demands for high-quality of services offered to users. Many researchers are investigating and developing multi-carrier modulations to meet certain key requirements for 5G wireless networks. Thus, the candidates multi-carrier modulation for 5G wireless networks techniques to overcome the identified limitations of the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) system are Filtered-Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (F-OFDM), Filter Bank Multicarrier (FBMC), and Universal Filtered Multi-carrier (UFMC). The objective of this paper is the performance evaluation of four candidate modulation formats for 5G wireless communication systems. Firstly, four communication systems OFDM, F-OFDM, FBMC, and UFMC are implemented under MATLAB software. Thereafter, the performance in terms of the Power Spectral Density (PSD), the Peak-to-average Power Ratio (PAPR), and the BER for the presented systems will be evaluated under different key parameters (Type of Modulation, Number of IFFT, Filters, etc.)

articleTitle: Sizing and Techno-Economic analysis of a Photovoltaic Solar System for a Primary School using PVSYST
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The investigating of the potential positive effects of incorporating renewable energy investments into the national grid involves providing schools with sustainable energy, seen as a valuable chance for investment. The paper aims to introduce a technical and economic feasibility study of implementing a dependable and cost-effective solar-powered generator in the northern Sahara region of Algeria at MEBAREK EL MILI school Laghouat. This system fulfills the school's energy requirements and sends excess energy to the grid using a smart meter, providing an alternative energy source while remaining connected to the main grid. The study employs PVSYST 7.3 to design and simulate the system using one year of electricity bill data at a 6 kW flow rate. Based on the system results and installation cost estimation, the repayment time can be projected.

articleTitle: Energy and Exergy Analysis of Combined Cooling, Heating and Power System using ORC and Ejector Refrigeration Cycle
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This study focuses on developing an efficient solar-geothermal hybrid system that can simultaneously provide cooling and power Utilizing organic Rankine cycle (ORC) in conjunction with the ejector refrigeration cycle (ERC). To ensure reliability, extensive evaluations of energy and exergy are conducted using R423A as the working fluid. The temperature range of the vapor generator is set from 180°C to 240°C to effectively utilize solar radiation as a heat source, while geothermal energy is harnessed at a temperature of 90°C. The analysis results demonstrate that the system, with R423A as the working fluid, achieves the lowest overall energy destruction and the highest energy efficiency, as well as notable exergy efficiency. Furthermore, a parametric analysis of the results highlights the significant impact of turbine inlet pressure and temperature of evaporator on key performance indicators such as power output, refrigeration capacity, energy efficiency and exergy efficiency of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Comparative Study and Optimization of MPPT Algorithms in a Standalone Photovoltaic Plant using Classical and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In recent years, various control methods for the Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT) of Photovoltaic (PV) systems have been proposed and evaluated in terms of energy efficiency, power conversion, dynamic performance, and reliability under different environmental conditions. Among these methods, those based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) are considered the best due to their stability and lack of requirement for prior information on the physical parameters. In this paper, a comparison between two PV systems using classical MPPT algorithms and Machine Learning (ML) algorithms has been conducted. This study introduces a novel angle to photovoltaic systems by conducting a comprehensive comparative analysis of Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT) algorithms. It innovatively contrasts classical techniques with emerging Machine Learning (ML) methods, rigorously evaluating them across energy efficiency, power conversion, and dynamic performance parameters. Through MATLAB/Simulink simulations, it demonstrates the superior performance of MLbased MPPT methods in stability, speed, and efficiency.

articleTitle: Prediction of Daily Global Solar Radiation in All Types of Sky Based on Sunshine Duration
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The development of any solar system requires necessarily a better knowledge of solar radiation. In the absence of this latter, the use of modeling to accomplish this task is increasingly becoming an unavoidable need. In this study, a proposed empirical model with four classical polynomial models and intelligent model such as the Support Vector Regression (SVR), were established, in order to express the horizontal global solar radiation (GHI) as a function of the insolation fraction σ. These models are evaluated and confronted for daily data which are recorded from Ghardaïa, in all type of skies. The experimental validation results revealed an excellent performance of the proposed model by an accuracy ranged between 3% and 4% and with correlation coefficient of 0.97. The comparative study shows that the proposed methods can compete with the usual models and even a machine learning approach in the prediction of GHI based on sunshine duration.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Power Supply Using 3 Types of Converters of a Discharge Lamp-Electronic Ballast System for Water Purification
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Water is a crucial resource that has been experiencing a continuous decline in quality over the years. Therefore, treating water has become a top priority, and the need to respect it has been recognized since ancient times. UV-c technology is an excellent solution that addresses both of these requirements effectively. The concept of UV bactericidal treatment involves the generation of ultraviolet rays inside a treatment chamber containing water. To ensure the effectiveness of UV-c disinfection, it is crucial to provide a reliable power supply to the low-pressure mercury-argon discharge lamps. In this research, the main objective is to determine the most optimal power source. To achieve this goal, the discharge lamp-electronic ballast system will be powered by three different types of converters. The first power supply utilizes a conventional converter, consisting of a half-bridge rectifier and inverter with PWM control. The second power supply employs a 4-cell serial multicell converter, which adopts a control strategy that modulates duty cycles. The third power supply is based on a single-phase matrix converter. In order to achieve the desired amplitude and frequency, a linear adjustment of the current is applied using a PI regulator. This approach aims to improve the quality of the current waveform and reduce total harmonic distortion (THD). The simulations for these power supply configurations were conducted using Matlab/Simpower system.

articleTitle: β-Ga2O3-Based Photodiode Performances Investigation: Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Recently, researcher's communities have concentrated on ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor-based materials with relatively wide band gaps ∼5eV. These materials have remarkable structural, optical and physical properties, for instance Gallium Oxide (GaO) and its phases present the most advantageous characteristics such as wide band gap (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>), high electrons mobility, interesting recombination life-time value and thermal stability in β-phase. In this work, a simulation of photodiode based on β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> semiconductor with Top contacts configuration was carried out using SILVACO TCAD software. Indeed, structural and optical aspects such as thickness, electrodes materials and illumination variation were investigated in terms of device electric performances. The obtained results denote a good agreement with precedent works relative to this field.

articleTitle: Stator Current Signal Analysing of Wind Turbine Generator For a Smart Fault Diagnosis Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The evolution of technologies, the progress of power electronics and economic stakes, the use of rotating machines is becoming increasingly important in all fields, including electrical drives and energy production. Their robustness, reliability and low cost are particularly appreciated. These generator-mode machines are the basis for the wind turbines of today. However, despite all the research and improvements that have been made, these machines still represent potential sites for stator and rotor failure. These faults need to be detected and located in good time, as they can cause serious damage to the system. In recent years, the diagnosis of faults affecting wind energy systems has been extensively studied. A large number of methods are available to improve system design, increase power quality and output, and reduce costs. Despite the results of this research, these multi-complex systems are still the subject of numerous laboratory research, both industrial and academic. The aim of this paper is to use knowledge-based methods, these methods do not use mathematical models to describe cause-and -effect relationships. The only knowledge is based on human experience through feedback. The aim is to generate healthy and faulty operating data for state variables and to use an advanced approach, based on deep learning, to detect and locate faults through stator current analysis.

articleTitle: Assessing Offshore Wind Resource for Sustainable Energy and Hydrogen Production in the El Kala Coastal Region
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This study aims to assess the offshore wind resources in Algeria's El Kala Coastal Region for sustainable energy and hydrogen production. Specifically, it evaluates the technical, economic, and environmental feasibility of installing a 300 MW offshore wind power plant in the Eastern region of Algeria. The wind analysis utilizes a WAsP-based model and incorporates hourly data collected at the El Kala meteorological station spanning from 2007 to 2021. Based on the results, El Kala has an important wind potential with average annual wind speed of 4.46 m/s corresponding to power density of 125 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Assuming a hub height of 150 m, the wind speed and power density increase to 8.18 m/s and 654 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. The remaining results for the offshore wind farm at El Kala are as follows: The annual energy production is 1275.7 GWh at 0.59 ∃/kWh. Furthermore, the hydrogen production amounts to 26767 tH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, with a cost of 1.43 ∃/kg. Importantly, the utilization of wind energy in El Kala leads to a significant reduction of approximately 557864 tons in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, aligning with sustainability objectives.

articleTitle: A Comparison Analysis between Two and Three Levels Inverter to Grid-Connected Used the Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This article presents a comparative study of two topologies of three-phase photovoltaic inverters connected to the grid, between the usual two-level inverter and three-level NPC (Neutral Point Clamped) inverter. Inverter control and the boost converter MPPT controller are based on the SRF-dq method and the INC algorithm respectively. The comparison relies on evaluating the overall efficiency and harmonic distortion of the inverter. All circuits are modeled and simulated using Matlab-Simulink. The results obtained indicate satisfaction with the quality, of the current and voltage injected into the electrical grid, and reflect that both inverters are efficient and comply with IEEE-519 standard recommendations, but the three-level inverter performs better results than the two-level inverter.

articleTitle: Behavior of Impedance and Phase of Mineral Oil after Successive Discharges in Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Power transformers play an irreplaceable role in power distribution and transmission networks. Diagnosis of transformer's degradation insulation system is of great importance in order to assess its performance and reliability. This paper discusses about the effect of applying simultaneous electrical discharges of low energy under AC voltage on the characteristics of the impedance and phase of the insulating mineral oil with frequency ranging from 20 Hz to 10 MHz. The impedance and phase are measured with a high precision LCR-meter where the insulation liquid is filled in the test cell with point-plane electrode system and a gap of 2.5 mm. The performed measurements provide a well correlation with the degree of degradation of the mineral oil and hence with its capacity and resistivity when submitted to AC high voltage discharges.

articleTitle: Modeling and Sizing a Battery for PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to describe and put into practice a technique called Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), which is frequently used in artificial intelligence to identify the best battery for a given set of requirements. We then expand our research to include electrical modelling of batteries. This research will be utilized to develop an ideal battery impedance model, which may then be examined later using, for instance, the impedance model's physical properties for diagnoses. Our strategy starts with dimensioning before moving on to modelling. We calculated the amount of errors to further validate our work. The novelty of our work can be summed up in the proof of the availability of a straightforward method for learning the battery's state of health.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of a LoRa Based Wireless Sensor Network for Low Power Localization in an Outdoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) and Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) have transformed industries by highlighting their crucial roles in sensing, communication, and data-driven decisions. One paramount feature in WSN is localization, enabling precise positioning of devices in real-world applications. Global Positioning Systems (GPS) have long been the mainstay of high-precision localization, but their high energy consumption is a significant obstacle to their seamless integration with low-power devices. In the quest for suitable solutions, Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWAN) have emerged as key players, providing energy-efficient connectivity. However, these advances raise questions about the localization accuracy within these networks. In this paper, we present the implementation of WSN based on Long Range (LoRa) technology to estimate the position of an object in an outdoor environment. We took advantage of LoRa technology to collect Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) measurements over a long distance. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is then trained on a collected dataset to estimate the 2-dimensional position of the object. The results show an estimate of the position with an average absolute error of 40.5 meters in an area of 360 meters by 360 meters. A web interface is made with Node-Red to monitor the position of the mobile object.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Dynamic Eccentricity Fault in Inverter-Fed Induction Machine Using Three Phase Stator Currents Intersection Signal
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The current research presents a dependable and practical indirect approach for detecting and diagnosing Dynamic Eccentricity in inverter-feed induction machines operating at varied load circumstances. The spectral analysis of the Three Phase Currents Intersection Signal (TPCIS) and its positive envelope is the main focus of the suggested technique. The sinusoidal TPCIS signal is extracted from finding time and amplitude of each positive and negative intersection point in three-phase stator current signals rather than using the classical Zero Crossing Time Approach (ZCTA), and the TPCIS signal is formed through searching and interpolating all the crossing points. The positive envelope of TPCIS can be obtained through spline interpolation of all positive crossing points. The theoretical foundation of the suggested technique is presented, and it is then experimentally confirmed by testing two induction machines: one healthy for comparison, and the other with Dynamic Eccentricity fault (DEF). Each machine is exposed to two loads (low, and high load). The acquired experimental findings illustrate the resilience and usefulness of the suggested approach, as well as its capacity to distinguish defective cases from healthy ones under varied load conditions, even at low load.

articleTitle: Control of Brushless Doubly-Fed Generator Using complex Coefficient PI Regulators
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Accurate brushless doubly fed induction machine (BDFIM) control is considered as a good alternative to traditional generators. In this study, a cascaded field oriented control based on complex coefficient PI regulators is investigated. The design of this control in the complex domain using both the positive and negative frequency information allows a triple objective: a decrease in the system dimension by half, a reduction in the control's scheme and a better stability margin of the control system as a whole. Simulations in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment are used in order to compare the effectiveness of the results with classic PI controller field-oriented control.

articleTitle: Pre-Feasibility Study and Control for Offshore Wind Farm in Algerian Coast
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This work presents a preliminary study on the possibility of establishing an offshore wind farm on the Algerian coast; For this purpose, we will select a location that can achieve the best productivity of the operation based on the documented geographical and climatic information. A station of a nominal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20MW$</tex> will be proposed; the system configuration, components, Control, and connection to the main grid, will be presented and simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. The results achieved are encouraging; It has been proven that offshore energy production in Algeria, which has not previously been considered, represents a promising choice.

articleTitle: Effect of Substrate Resistivity on Spiral Inductor in Radio Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: SOI(Silicon-on-Insulator)technology, considering its development and benefits compared to silicon Bulk technology, is considered very promising to meet the increased demands of the wireless telecommunications market in terms of low cost, CMOS compatibility, low substrate losses, and low power consumption system-on-chip manufacturing capability. Thus, best-in-class Si-based substrates, additionally high performance RF components are in high demand. The porous silicon (PSi) substrate holds great promise for emerging wireless communication integrated circuits demanding the elimination significant attenuation at high frequencies in the bulk silicon substrate. It is within this context that, the work aims to demonstrate the applicability of the porous silicon substrate for the design of RF circuits operating in radio frequency band. An inductor is integrated, and a comparison between the performances of this RF band inductor in terms of S-parameters (insertion losses) and of quality factor on the substrates studied is developed.

articleTitle: Secure Turbo Code Design Based on Chaotic Interleavers
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper is a proposal for a secure turbo code design based on chaotic interleavers, employing general symmetric unimodal maps. This interleaving process introduces randomness and confusion, making it more challenging for unauthorized parties to decode the encoded data. Secure turbo codes based on chaotic interleavers are a promising approach to physical layer security.

articleTitle: Base-station node implementation for real-time IoT/WSN Applications: Case of RSSI-based outdoor localisation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The presented paper proposes a model of the Internet of Things (IoT) based Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) base station node for outdoor localisation. The node is supposed to be an essential part of the network's infrastructure, where the node should be adapted to the real-time application. This study suggested designing and implementing a base-station sensor node for data collection and trilateration localisation processing. The proposed node is implemented on an FPGA type to utilise the power and speed of this type of circuit in a pure hardware description or a combined hardware/software approach, using languages like C/C++ to describe materials known as a high-level synthesis (HLS) approach. The node incorporates in its architecture a MicroBlaze-type soft-processor to manage tasks like transmission between the different end-device nodes, presenting data at the inputs of the Ip-core for processing, and reading and representing output data. An additional trilateration block has been built as a dedicated IP core for the localisation process. The experimental findings confirmed that the proposed base station node could perform real-time data processing as expected, where a time of 63 microseconds was reached in the RSSI-based outdoor localisation process.

articleTitle: A Novel Modified Improved Propotionnate Fast NLMS Algorithm for Acoustic Echo Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The Modified Improved Proportionate Normalized Least Mean Square (m-IPNLMS) algorithm enhanced the performance of the original IPNLMS algorithm by establishing a relationship between an important parameter known as the proportional term and the sparseness measure built on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\ell}_2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\ell}_1$</tex> norms. To further improve the performance of the m-IPNLMS algorithm, we propose first, to extend the Fast NLMS concept to the m-IPNLMS algorithm and then, by using the sparseness measure based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\ell}_1, \boldsymbol{\ell}_2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\ell}_\infty$</tex> norms, which provide adequate representations of both dispersive and sparse impulse responses, we also replace the quadratic output filtering error with a recursive estimation version. The proposed algorithm, called Novel-Modified IPNLMS (Novel-m-IPNLMS) algorithm is superior in terms of convergence speed, tracking ability and steady-state mean square error (MSE) for sparse and dispersive systems. Simulation results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the suggested algorithm.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Epidemic DTN Routing on Low-Power and Lossy Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Delay Tolerant Networks (DTNs) are well-suited for environments with limited network coverage or high congestion, thanks to their ability to adapt to intermittent connectivity and delays. On the other hand, Low-power and Lossy Networks (LLNs) face limitations in computation, memory, and energy,. This paper explores the possibility of deploying DTN routing protocols over LLNs, scenarios such as healthcare, post-disaster management, and remote or rural areas. The present study explores the effectiveness of deploying Epidemic routing algorithm over LLNs. Our simulation results indicate that maintaining moderate Time-to-Live (TTL) values enables Epidemic routing to maintain high packet delivery and low packet loss rates even for large LLN sizes. This trend holds in the presence of mobile nodes.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Predictive Controller for Trajectory Tracking of Differential-Drive Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a fuzzy predictive control approach for nonholonomic mobile robots. To achieve this objective, we introduce an innovative strategy to address specific challenges that emerge when utilizing linear models for nonholonomic mobile robots. The approach employed involves extending the error model through the integration of a Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy logic system. By considering various values of dynamic behavior, multiple linear error models are derived, providing the groundwork for formulating the T-S fuzzy model. Importantly, the resulting fuzzy model maintains alignment with the original model while simultaneously enhancing its precision. The practical effectiveness of our proposed methodology is demonstrated through its application in guiding a nonholonomic mobile robot along a predefined reference path within two distinct tracking scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimizing Power Flow in Algeria's Adrar Power System Using BHO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The meta-heuristic methods are very efficient for the search of global solution for complex problems and BHO (Black Hole Optimizer) algorithm is one of them. The aim of this project is applying (BHO) algorithm on the Adrar power system with wind power generation (WPG) in order to solve the optimal power flow (OPF) dispatch, fuel cost minimization, and reducing emissions, It is evident that the use of the algorithm can contribute to improving the efficiency and performance of energy systems and improving environmental sustainability by improving power flow and fuel cost minimization and emissions. The findings of this study provide insights into the effectiveness of the BHO algorithm in improving the Adrar power system while achieving the desired objectives.

articleTitle: Comparative investigation on electrical discharges temporal parameters between air and transformer mineral oil
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The paper deals with investigating electrical discharges currents and voltages drop measurements in pointplane electrode system in air and mineral oil, and examines their temporal characteristics and behavior. The study focuses on the impact of electrical discharges on the energy dissipated between the electrodes, which plays a crucial role in the severity of the occurred discharges. Indeed, power transformers are susceptible to lightning strikes and switching surges, which can result in insulation degradation, overheating, and even failure. The experimental design involves analyzing the current, voltage and energy variations in time of electrical discharges in both air and mineral oil to identify each of them. The results show that mineral oil requires higher voltage levels for electrical discharges compared to air due to its better insulating properties. The wave generated by electrical discharges propagates faster in air than in mineral oil. These findings enhance our understanding of electrical discharges and their effects on transformers, contributing to the development of prevention and mitigation measures for reliable and safe power system operation.

articleTitle: Impact of Training Algorithms on Faults Detection of PV Panel
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Photovoltaic systems have become essential in the production of electrical energy. They offer green and renewable energy. Research is ongoing to make them more competitive and available. In this context and to enrich the literature dedicated to the promotion and development of photovoltaic systems, we have developed this comparative study on learning algorithms namely: Levenberg-Marquardt, scaled conjugate gradient and Bayesian regularization. The comparison is made according to the value of the coefficient of determination of each algorithm. The results obtained show that the choice of the learning algorithm in the diagnosis of solar panel faults using fitting neural network is decisive.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of SVM, Venturini, and PWM with Three Intervals Modulation Techniques for the Control of an AC/AC Three-Phase Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of three modulation techniques, namely SVM (Space Vector Modulation), Venturini, and PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) with three intervals, for controlling an AC/AC three-phase matrix converter. The study aims to evaluate the performance and effectiveness of these strategies in achieving accurate control and efficient energy conversion. The analysis includes a comprehensive examination of key parameters such as output voltage quality, total harmonic distortion (THD), power factor, and switching losses. Simulations results are utilized to compare the performance of the different strategies under various operating conditions. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each technique, enabling researchers and practitioners to make informed decisions in selecting the most suitable control strategy for AC/AC three-phase matrix converters.

articleTitle: Digital Twins for Health Care Monitor: Baby Incubator Temperature and Humidity Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Digital Twin has gained significant attention in recent years as a promising approach to bridge the physical and digital realms, enabling virtual representations of real-world assets and systems, and its application in healthcare is transforming the way medical devices are designed, operated, and monitored. This paper presents an introduction to the integration of digital twin technology with Amazon AWS for healthcare purpose, a leading cloud computing platform, using ESP32 and DHT22 sensor as proposed solution for Baby Incubator temperature and humidity monitoring. The combination of Arduino's hardware and software capabilities with the scalability and analytical power of AWS allows for real-time monitoring, data collection, and analysis of environmental conditions. This paper explores the fundamental concepts of digital twins applied on healthcare, highlights the capabilities of the ESP32 with DHT22 sensor, outlines the integration process with Amazon AWS, and discusses the potential applications and benefits of this Integrated solution.

articleTitle: Low-complexity Architecture for Cognitive Radio
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Every day, electromagnetic radio spectrums become precious and expensive. Cognitive radios represent one of the best solutions to improve the available radio frequency (RF) spectrum utilization. Since many forms of communication do not utilize the allocated spectrum fully. So, dynamic detection of no utilized spectrum is crucial. Generally, energy sensing and cyclostationary feature sensing are the most used techniques. Traditional cyclostationary feature-sensing signal correlations are implemented by a complex adder and complex multiplier, which requires significant memory space to store filter coefficients and increased hardware usage. To overcome the above-mentioned problems, a complex pipelined multiply and adder architecture is designed to reduce the area occupancy further. In this research, complex multiplication is designed using two absolute multipliers. The proposed architecture is coded using VHDL on a Virtex-5 Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) device, and the results are compared with similar works. The implementation demonstrates that the proposed operator can reduce FPGA logic requirements with a high maximum working frequency.

Author Keywords: Finite impulse response Field Programmable Gate Array

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Smart Irrigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Smart irrigation systems have revolutionized the farming industry by utilizing modern innovations to optimize water usage and handle water scarcity issues. The performance of two machine learning algorithms, Decision Tree and Support Vector Machines (SVM), in categorizing irrigation status in smart irrigation systems is evaluated in this research. The goal is to detect whether or not specified areas or plants have been watered, which is critical for proper irrigation management. Sensors in smart irrigation systems detect environmental data such as temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and rainfall. The obtained data is processed using machine learning methods to classify the irrigation status. For training and evaluation, this study makes use of a large dataset from a real-world smart irrigation system. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of both the Decision Tree and SVM algorithms. Decision Tree excels in terms of precision and recall, allowing for the accurate detection of hydrated and non-watered areas or plants. SVM achieves good accuracy and F1-score, allowing for a complete evaluation of irrigation status. These findings promote smart irrigation systems by emphasizing the importance of machine learning methods for accurate irrigation status classification. The findings help stakeholders choose appropriate algorithms for efficient water management and support sustainable agriculture practices.

articleTitle: Percentile-Based Estimator for Generalized Rayleigh CFAR Ship Detection in SAR Imagery
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging is a valuable tool for remote sensing, offering insights into complex environments. SAR images often, though, contain clutter from natural and man-made structures, making accurate target detection difficult. To overcome this challenge, we introduce, for complex Generalized Rayleigh (GR) environments, a Constant False Censoring Rate (CFCR) algorithm based on the Percentile Estimator (PCE) along with a Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection algorithm, yielding the PCE-CFAR detector. In doing this, based on the assumption of a homogenous middle half set of pixels within the Sliding Reference Window (SRW), we first propose closed-form expressions for the lower and upper censoring thresholds using the PCE. Then, upon censoring the undesirable data at both ends, we employ the remaining dataset to estimate the unknown distribution parameters via the same expressions of the PCE used in the censoring algorithm, and so the detection threshold closed-form expression. Finally, through a series of experimentations and comparisons with existing techniques, we showcase the effectiveness and resilience of the proposed ship target detector in real SAR images.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Microbiological and Physicochemical Characteristics of Solar-Dried Allium Sativum L in the Adrar Region: A Study of Quality and Safety Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Garlic (Allium sativum L) is a plant that is widely used in cooking in different types, fresh, pickled, and dried, additionally in medicinal effects, however, little research studied the properties of physicochemical and microbiological of garlic after treatment with solar drying. In the present work, dried garlic was brought to determine the physicochemical properties including Moisture content, ash content, the dosage of fat, the dosage of protein, and the total dosage of sugars.in addition, microbiological analysis such as Mesophilic aerobic bacteria, total and fecal coliforms, Enterobacteriaceae, Yeast, and molds. The results showed that the solar dried garlic saved the same properties physicochemical compared to the literature on fresh garlic, then, for the microbiological analysis, we note some colonies of Mesophilic aerobic bacteria and yeasts and molds that didn't have any risk to human health a. In conclusion, solar drying is a method that promotes for conservation of post-harvest products without any degradation of nutritive value and is apt for human consumption

articleTitle: New Induction Motor Fault Detection Method at No-Load Level Employed to Start Diagnosis of Anomalies
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Among the techniques widely employed to analyse the induction motor health condition is the motor current signal analysis, which effectively extracts the characteristic frequencies related to fault at a high load levels.
