However, this technique failed to detect faults at low and no-load levels. Moreover, when using an inverter to feed the induction motor, it is challenging to detect faults even at high load levels. In this context, the present work aims to propose a new fault detection method, which helps to determine the health state of this engine at no-load condition through a scatter plot of positive current sequence in terms of zero sequence after making Fortescue transformation. Then, Artificial Neuron Network (ANN) uses as an input only one statistical feature to the identifier and classifier of different induction motor conditions. The practical results are interesting, promising and effective to apply in real industrial sectors.

articleTitle: Management Stand-alone Hybrid Renewable Energy System Based on Wind and Solar with Battery Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper describes the management of a standalone hybrid energy system (HES) based on two renewable sources. The sun, wind. and the battery supports the system. Solar panels and wind turbines (WT) connected with permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSG) were used for power production. Power converters have been used together with control algorithms for efficient power management. The filters were used to dispose of the largest amount of harmonics in the inverter. The proposed model provides a strategy for managing energy under various generating conditions. In order to save energy for a fixed load. Proposed hybrid accession simulated with MATLAB/Simulink

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Visual Navigation Systems using Optical Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper aims to introduce navigation frameworks that rely on visual perception for a mobile robot equipped with wheels, executed through optical flow methodologies. Two discriminant algorithms are investigated to analyze visual cues in unfamiliar static environments. The control systems proposed rely on estimations of movement and decision-making mechanisms that use the measured data calculated by the optical inflow algorithms to direct the robot autonomously within its working area. The results are analyzed and explored, to showcase the capacity for unimpeded movement by a mobile robot using visually-based navigation systems, without any collisions with obstructions.

articleTitle: Parameters Identification of Induction Motor Using the Slime Mould Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This research work focuses on estimating the parameters of an induction motor (IM) using recent algorithm: The slime mould algorithm (SMA). The SMA algorithm shows the stability of this algorithm to search large areas with a high accuracy. Compared to the particle swarm optimization (PSO), the simulation results indicate that the performance of SMA in terms of both accuracy and convergence speed makes it the algorithm of choice for estimating IM parameters.

articleTitle: An Improved Delay Time Of Optical Half-Adder Applying Nonlinear Photonic Crystals Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In the present investigation, we attempt to develop a new structure of optical half adder using nonlinear photonic crystal ring resonator. As a main advantage, the use of coupling between bus waveguide and ring resonator increases the power intensity of the output and opens a wider photonic band gap (PBG). In this design, in order to improve the optical characteristics of the designed half adder, the combination of interference-based defect and nonlinear Kerr effect is exploited, as well as logic function transmit power control, including radius and refractive index of coupling rods. As a result, the structure contrast ratio is valued between 12.74 dB and 16.33 dB, proportional to the output power, which varies between 1.7% to 5% and 88 % to 108% for logic level “0” and “1” respectively. Resulting a minimum threshold power around of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3\ \mathrm{W}/\mu\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>. Additionally, the suggested design can be taken into account for ultra-fast integrated circuits to assure their integration in optical communication networks. Plane wave expansion (PWE) and finite difference time domain (FDTD), two distinct numerical techniques, are applied to estimate the propagation modes and the output spectrum respectively.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Analysis of Multi-Mega-Scale Off-Grid Photovoltaic-Hydrogen Production System
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The importance of producing green hydrogen from renewable energy sources is increased with the growing need of clean energy carriers. This research focuses on the Algiers potential to generate green hydrogen using multi-mega-scale off-grid photovoltaic-hydrogen system to serve hydrogen users. To obtain the lowest Levelized Cost Of Hydrogen (LCOH), the system is investigated and optimized utilizing a three-objective approach including total hydrogen deficit and energy dump possibility. A dynamic power and hydrogen management strategy is used for the control of the system. The short-term (2025) cost scenario is applied. Eighteen feasible solutions has been addressed. The worst and best solutions gives LCOH of 18.24 ∃/kg and 11.89 ∃/kg, respectively.

articleTitle: Printed Monopole Antenna Design for Early Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to design a simple miniaturized microstrip antenna and detect variations in its reflection response to locate tumors in the human brain. The proposed antenna has a size of 36×32×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. This antenna is designed to operate at a resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz, which align with the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. The designed antenna has an omnidirectional radiation pattern with a maximum gain of about 1.43 dBi. For the intended application, numerical simulations are performed using a tumor with a radius of 5 mm. The reflection response of the proposed antenna is investigated for two cases: one without a tumor and another with a tumor placed at three different positions inside the brain. When there is no tumor present, the resonance frequency is similar to that of an antenna in open space. However, in the presence of a tumor, there is a shift and increase in the resonance frequency, which is directly proportional to the distance between the antenna and the head. This shift serves as an indication of the presence of a tumor.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Voltage Control of Uninterruptible Power Supply with an Output RLC Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In response to the growing demand for advanced control techniques tailored to three-phase inverters equipped with output filters, aiming to produce high-quality voltage while minimizing total harmonic distortion (THD), model predictive control (MPC) emerges as a highly effective solution. Despite being an intuitive controller that is easily understandable and implementable, it has a significant drawback: MPC has mainly been applied to slow dynamic systems due to the substantial number of complex calculations needed to solve the optimization problem at each sampling interval. The objective of this paper is to implement MPC with both one-step and two-step prediction, considering linear and non-linear loads. The proposed control strategy is verified through simulation using MATLAB/Simulink tools.

articleTitle: Automated Fruits Inspection and Sorting Smart System for Industry 4.0 Based on OpenCV and PLC
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Sorting fruits individually by hand is one of the most exhausting tasks. It involves a great deal of work and labor, as well as a great deal of time. Automation and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques have enhanced product consistency, increased production, and decreased operational expenses. In this context, an automated fruits inspection and sorting system based on PLC (programmable logic controller) and OpenCV is proposed in this paper. The S7-1200 PLC of Siemens was used to manage the operational portion of the system. A Python-based OpenCV algorithm was developed to detect and calculate the size of fruits using a camera and communicate decisions to the PLC using Snap7 ethernet communication to sort them. The solution proposed was validated with a realized prototype. Remote monitoring and control were achieved using a Human Machine Interface (HMI) based on SIMATIC WinCC of Siemens.

articleTitle: Study of three different optimization algorithms to calculate the optimal switching angles for the SHEPWM modulation method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Selective harmonic elimination pulse width modulation (SHEPWM) is a popular modulation strategy that controls DC/AC converters. It is a powerful technic because of its ability to eliminate undesired harmonics and work on low switching frequency which increases the lifespan of the switching devices, lowers the switching losses, and also provides a high output quality voltage. The main objective of this paper is to study three optimization algorithms genetic algorithm, generalized pattern search, and particle swarm optimization for how they improve the SHEPWM method to produce a better output quality voltage with eliminated harmonics by calculating different sets of the switching angles. The results of this study are validated on a five and seven-level Cascaded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}$</tex>-bridge inverter.

articleTitle: All Optical AND Logic Gate Based on Nonlinear Kerr Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Our study has been focused on a new design of an All optical AND logic gate based on a nonlinear Kerr effect and a photonic crystal ring resonator (PhCRR). Thus, we have designed and simulated a new optical switch which function with the nonlinear Kerr effect to obtain the switching intensity and the maximum transmission efficiency. These structures proposed PhCRR, function in the telecommunication wavelength of 1585nm and gives a high transmission efficiency of 100% with the threshold power obtained for this structure is 0.35kw/μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The AND logic gate exhibits a good performance like the contrast ration and the response time. The Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) and Plane Wave Expansion (PWE) approaches have been used to model this operation, which have been used to investigate the performance of our proposed of AND logic gate structure.

articleTitle: Solar Outdoor Light Study [Design, PV System Dimensioning and Photonic Studies]
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Renewable, green or even clear energies, all this terms refers to the unlimited natural sources of energy used most generally on electricity generation. The rate of consumption of these sources is very low comparing to their availability the thing that makes them a good alternative and replacement of oils and Fossils fuels resources. The main purpose of this paper is the presentation of a new design of a solar outdoor light. This new design allows this proposed system of achieving its main function which is lighting the outdoor surfaces and also helps in the generation of extra energy that can be used for feeding other parts such as connection Wi-Fi or network antenna or any other accessories required by the customer. For this solar outdoor light, three studies were hold, a conception and resistance study of its body, a dimensioning of the installed photovoltaic and storage system and a photonic study configuration. And for all the mentioned above studies, they were judged satisfying and conform to the required norms while ensuring a high factors of resistance and stability, a high durability and even a low economic cost on the long term time.

articleTitle: Infrared Image Stripe Noise Removal by Solving First-And Second-Order Total Variation Inverse Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Stripe noise is a prominent type of noise in infrared imaging systems. It has a unique directional property where it usually appears as vertical lines imposed on the image. This paper introduces an algorithm that turns an image denoising problem into solving inverse problems for each row of the noisy image, giving users a powerful tool for destriping infrared images. This was done by integrating first- and second-order total variation (TV) regularizations, which has led to excellent denoising capabilities around edges and smooth areas. The algorithm's performance is carefully examined, along with comparisons to other denoising techniques, using simulated and real-world data, emphasizing the algorithm's superiority in terms of noise reduction and reconstruction accuracy. Comparing the proposed method to state-of-the-art techniques, it shows greater performance in improving the visual quality of the produced image.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Slot Antenna for Miniaturized Biomedical Implants
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper presents a compact-size antenna designed for biomedical implants. The antenna operates at the dual-band of 910 MHz and 2.45 GHz, which fall within the industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band ranges. The proposed antenna achieves a significant size reduction with a minimal form factor measuring only 17.64 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(7 mm × 7 mm × 0.36 mm). This size reduction is accomplished by employing a printed antenna with a dual spiral-shape slot and incorporating an inverted U structure, contributing to a more compact design. Additionally, a superstrate layer is introduced to enhance the impedance matching and compactness of the antenna further. The proposed antenna showcases several notable attributes, such as its miniaturization, dual-band operation, and commendable gain values compared to alternative implantable antennas. To evaluate its performance, the antenna is simulated within a multi-layered enclosure comprised of skin, fat, and muscle. The proposed antenna's SARs (specific absorption rates) are calculated within the human tissue model at both operating frequencies. This analysis provides insights into the electromagnetic energy absorption by the surrounding tissues, ensuring the antenna's safety for use in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Low Cost ECT Based System for Thickness Measurement of Metallic Plates
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This contribution focuses on the nondestructive testing of the thickness of metallic plates, using eddy current testing. Specifically, we present a low cost device for measuring the thickness of metal plates without contact, while maintaining a high accuracy appropriate for industrial applications. The proposed device consists mainly of two eddy current sensors, a realized electronic circuit and a developed Labview interface. In order to test the lift-off effect, three aluminum samples with thicknesses of 6, 12.5 and 19.5 mm were prepared on three different positions between the two sensors. the experimental measurements for the thickness of plates have been carried out for the verification of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Identifying Broken Rotor Bars in Squirrel Cage Induction Motors: Examination of Statistical Characteristics Derived from Start-Up Current Envelope
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In today's context, condition monitoring has risen to prominence as a critical facet in resolving issues pertaining to electrical machines. This has led to a substantial acceleration in research focused on fault diagnosis, specifically in the realm of induction motors. This paper aims to integrate the concept of broken bar faults into a squirrel cage induction motor, a procedure that requires continuous conditioning. The identification of rotor bar faults during the steady-state operation of induction motors is accomplished via the stator current envelope. Variations in this envelope are employed as a diagnostic feature indicative of fault conditions. Many global studies concentrate on the diagnosis and detection of rotor faults, as well as a range of feature extraction methodologies, such as the analysis of the starting current envelope. The effectiveness of the stator current envelope is highlighted through comparisons between the outcomes of this experimental system and those derived from a healthy induction motor.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Control Strategies for Passivity-Based VSI in Microgrids Between Conventional Droop Control and Droop Control with Two Integrators
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: As energy demands in microgrids have expanded, parallel-connected distributed generators are needed to fulfill the load users' demand. By combining the frequency and voltage of inverter-based generators, this study analyzes two essential control systems in microgrids: conventional droop control and Droop Control with two Integrators. This work will give a comparative analysis of control techniques regarding stability, control flexibility, transient mode and implementation complexity in a passivity-based voltage source inverter (VSI) under various scenarios and load types. The effectiveness of these strategies is demonstrated using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Impact of Distributed Generation on Voltage Profile in Distribution Systems: A Current Mismatch based Load Flow Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Conventional load flow methods modifications are necessary when taking into account the integration of distributed generations (DG) in electric distribution systems. In the present work, the impact of the DG's operating modes (PQ-PV) on the voltage profile when considering changes in their sizes and locations is studied. The load flow based current injection mismatches is proposed. The ten-bus test distribution system is used for validation purposes. Different scenarios are considered and some corresponding results are discussed.

articleTitle: Real Time Drones Detection Based on Cameras and Recent YOLO Algorithm Versions
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The present paper focused on the real time drones detection using the computer vision algorithm You Only Look Once (YOLO), profiting of its several versions, such as YOLOv5 and YOLOv8. In our work, we used the smallest YOLO versions in order to have the real time aspect (small (s) versions). Training, validation and test processes were done on a customized dataset. The investigated YOLO versions was compared using different metrics such as precision, recall, mAP and box-loss. Furthermore, models were optimized in order to ensure the real time aspect. OpenVino and ONNX optimizer were used, the optimization results of different models are presented, in order to find the best model for the real-time requirements. A comparative synthesis between the different models in terms of precision and inference time is carried out, in order to have the best model in terms of drones detection efficiency and in real time. YOLOv5s has a mAP of 98% and a inference time of 31F P S and YOLOv8s has a mAP of 98.6% and an inference time of 20F P S. Which makes YOLOv5s is the best model for real time drones detection.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Synchronous Reluctance Generator in Grid-Connected Wind Energy Conversion Systems: A Comprehensive Feasibility Study and Control Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This research investigates the control of a grid-connected wind energy conversion system (WECS), which uses different types of generators, such as permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs) and doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs). However, the high cost of rare earth materials in PMSGs and the rotor losses associated with DFIGs have led to the exploration of the synchronous reluctance generator (SynRG) as a promising alternative. The SynRG is an attractive option because it is robust, simple, and cost-effective. It does not have a rotor cage, windings, or magnets. This paper studies the feasibility of integrating a SynRG into a WECS, with a specific focus on the 11kW SynRM and a wind turbine prototype. The converted wind energy is injected into the grid using a back-to-back converter. The speed control of the SynRG is based on maximum power point tracking technology. A rectifier connected to the generator regulates the DC bus voltage. The control of active and reactive power is achieved using a conventional PI-based field-oriented control (FOC) strategy, employing an inverter connected to the grid. The proposed system and control scheme are demonstrated through meticulous numerical simulations conducted using the MATLAB/Simulink software. The simulation results show that the SynRG can efficiently convert energy across the entire wind speed range within the turbine's tolerance. In conclusion, this study shows that the SynRG is a viable option for WECSs. It is cost-effective, has a robust structure, and is simple. The paper effectively demonstrates the proposed system and control strategy, providing valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field.

articleTitle: Thermal Conductivity in a Nanofluid Filled Transformer: Modeling by the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Nanofluids (NFs) are insulating fluids that have improved heat transfer capabilities compared to conventional insulating fluids used in power transformers. In this work, the focus is on the thermal conductivity and heat transfer of NFs based on mineral and vegetable oils, where the finite element method (FEM) was used to model the thermal conductivity of NFs and compare them with the base fluid (BF) for a temperature range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$293\ K$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$393\ K$</tex>. The nanoparticles (NPs) used in the study are titanium dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({Ti{O}_2})$</tex> NPs with different concentrations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0\%,0.004\%$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.01\%)$</tex>, the results showed a significant improvement in heat flux with the addition NPs. The thermal conductivity of NFs also increased compared to base fluids, but with increasing temperature, the heat transfer performance of all samples decreased.

articleTitle: Intelligent Transport System (ITS) for Healthcare: Smart Ambulance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: While Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) have already produced considerable advancements in traffic management and safety conditions, its direct application in the healthcare sector opens up new opportunities for improving ambulance services. We will propose an ambulance directing system based on hospital medical equipment in this paper. We hope to reduce patient treatment delays, maximize resource usage, and lower the risks associated with eventual patient diversion owing to a lack of adequate medical equipment by addressing this critical component. We will rely on the SVM method to classify and on Google Maps to choose the best routes. The results showed a high accuracy in the classification, reaching 100 percent, and the use of Google Map greatly facilitated the process of choosing the most appropriate routes. In the future, we aim to expand the data set and use Artificial Intelligence methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Multi Connectivity Datalogger using SD Card Storage for Photovoltaic System Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The design and construction of a low-cost datalogger for remote monitoring of stand-alone solar systems are presented in this work. It satisfies accuracy standards, uses open-source hardware and software, and stores data on an SD card. It uses an Arduino Uno board, a SD card for data storage, Bluetooth and USB for data transfer, and a Windows application for data analysis. A solar photovoltaic system's electrical and meteorological characteristics will be monitored and recorded. The Arduino Uno board was selected as the microcontroller platform due to its wide availability and simplicity. A DS1307 Real-Time Clock (RTC) chip is included in the system for precise date and time stamps related to data that is saved in the SD card. the windows application is developed to make data analysis and visualisation easier. With the help of this application, users may perform data processing and storage, get data from the datalogger to a PC via USB or Bluetooth, and create graphical representations of the logged parameters. This application provides an intuitive user interface for simple communication with the datalogger system. The use of the suggested datalogger system offers a reliable and affordable method for tracking and studying solar installations. The logging, storing, transferring, and visualising of data are made possible, which helps with the overall administration and optimisation of solar energy systems.

articleTitle: Nonlinear control via Backstepping for five-phase permanent magnet synchronous generator-based wind generation system
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper presents a design for one of the nonlinear control techniques for wind-generation system (WGS) connected to the distribution grid, as this system is based on a five-phase permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG). To achieve the connection between the generation system and the grid we use two converters that are installed consecutive and a capacitor acting as a DC link between them. The main objective of this work is to apply the backstepping control (BSC) strategy to this system to improve wind power extraction and maintain the performance stability of the generator under variable wind speed. The main contribution of this paper is the comparison of two nonlinear control technologies, second order sliding mode (SOSMC) and backstepping (BSC), where SOSMC is characterized by a rapid dynamic response and insensitivity to parameter changes, concerning BSC is designed based on the law for Lyapunov that provides better stability to the system with stable performance. In order to verify the performance of the proposed control strategy, we use Matlab simulation software, where the simulation results show a distinct performance of this technique.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Energy Management System with Appliance Scheduling for a Solar Home Based on a Programmable Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This article presents the development of a Solar Home Energy Management System (SHEMS). The proposed SHEMS architecture aims to optimize the use of locally generated photovoltaic electricity to provide the home's energy requirements. Loads planning has been added to the energy flow management. An S7-1200 Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) is used to implement the energy management algorithm. Several PV production and load consumption scenarios were considered to evaluate the SHEMS. The results show that optimal load scheduling can achieve advantageous energy cost savings for the owners by satisfying the demand directly from the PV generator and peak shaving allows for net-work relief. Depending on the season, managing loads improves selfconsumption rates by 1% to 11% and lowers summer peak consumption by about 1.4kWh/d.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Energy Conversion and Its Applications: Sensors and Actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Piezoelectric sensors and actuators have gained significant attention in recent years due to their unique ability to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy and vice versa. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the principles, applications, and advancements in the field of piezoelectric sensors and actuators. It discusses the underlying working principles, materials used, fabrication techniques, and various applications in different industries. Additionally, it highlights the challenges and future prospects for further development in this rapidly evolving field. Recent advancements in the field of piezoelectric sensors and actuators include the development of flexible and wearable devices, integration with wireless communication technologies, and miniaturization for micro- and nanoscale applications. However, challenges such as hysteresis, temperature dependence, and long-term stability of piezoelectric materials still need to be addressed to enhance the performance and reliability of these devices.

articleTitle: Heat Flux Distribution on the Receiver of a Linear Fresnel Reflector Designed for Desalination
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This work presents a numerical study focused on optical and geometric evaluations for completing the construction and determining the dimensions of a linear Fresnel solar collector prototype with a cylindrical-parabolic secondary reflector employed for desalination. The study analyzes the distribution of solar flux around the absorber tube on three selected days throughout the year in the climate conditions of Algerian city “Blida” using the SolTrace program and the Monte Carlo method. The obtained results indicate that the concentrator was successfully validated and has good optical performance., as indicated by the homogeneity of heat flux over the absorber surface.

articleTitle: Study and Design a Low-Power Water Meter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: At this time, the issue of water scarcity and stress presents a significant and pressing danger to the global population[1]. To conserve water wealth, we must adopt modern controlling and monitoring consumption management techniques. Due to the smart meter, we can automate consumption readings in a distribution network. This work consists of the development of a water meter easy to implement and transmits the volume readings to visualize it in a user interface based on Node-Red. The contribution of this water meter is realizing an intelligent system based on a battery that allows it to prolong its lifespan of it, as long as possible by using a switching circuit between the turbine generator, and the battery that supplies the system in sleep mode. The meter is equipped with a flow detector that wakes up the MCU from sleep mode and also has a flow sensor that allows us to calculate the volume. Through the LoRa module the meter transmits the information to a gateway. To extend the longevity of the battery, we have implemented a circuit that allows seamless switching between the generator and the battery as needed. Additionally, we have incorporated other circuits that effectively disable all system components during sleep mode, minimizing power consumption to the bare minimum. These measures contribute significantly to conserving energy and ensuring optimal battery performance, providing a sustainable and reliable solution for our system.

articleTitle: Development of Automatic Nutrient Dosing System for Hydroponics
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Fertigation is a method used in agriculture to provide water-soluble nutrients through irrigation. It is crucial to correctly adjust the machine and nozzles to apply the right amount of liquid fertilizer per hectare. This work aims to automatically maintain a specific amount of the major nutrients, such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and several micronutrients, for their normal growth and development. In the present work, an automatic system is proposed to control the quality of organic and inorganic fertilizers, considering all the measurable essential parameters like pH, electrical conductivity, and temperature with automatic temperature compensation to arrive at an adequate nutritive solution for the cultivated plant.

articleTitle: Neural Network Model Predictive Control Based on PSO Approach: Applied to DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: A control approach based on neural network identification and particle swarm optimization algorithm is depicted in this work. The proposed control technique, called neural network model predictive control optimized by the particles swarm optimization algorithm, has been tested in simulation, to control the rotation speed of a direct current motor. This control technique proved its effectiveness in terms of accuracy (analysis of the value of the root mean square error, the mean square error, and the absolute mean square error) and overshoot through a comparative study between the simulation results obtained by the proposed controller and a PID controller tuned by the teaching learning based optimization algorithm, using a multi-step and sinusoïdal reference trajectories to represent the desired rotational speed.

articleTitle: DPC Control for Grid-Tied Inverter Powered by PV System Under Change of Parameters and Load
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Renewable energy exploitation is rapidly increasing, especially for global electricity production. Numerous enhancements are carried out to improve the exploitation of these renewable sources by using advanced power converters on one hand or adopting new control approaches on the other hand. In this regard, this paper deals with a PV system that is controlled by Direct Power Control (DPC) for the AC side on one hand, and a Fuzzy Logic Controller to extract the maximum power on the other hand. The performance of the presented system is validated through simulation tests using MATLAB.

articleTitle: Complex Medium Permittivity Retrieval Based on Curvature Calculation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper concerns the estimation of the refractive index of a complex medium from tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) data. It is based on curvature calculation which is due the assumption of vacuum propagation velocity through the medium during the signal focusing process. A mathematical modelling is developed so as to depict the propagation of electromagnetic waves in a complex medium. It takes into account properties such as thickness, wave propagation velocity and refractive index. Furthermore, the developed modelling technique is used to calculate the curvature and compare it with the curvature observed in Tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) image. The results clearly illustrate that the refractive index can be accurately estimated with a minimal error rate of 6%.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of an Intelligent System Control of the Elbow Prosthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The number of people having undergone an amputation of one or more limbs is on the permanent increase, among these amputations we are interested in humeral. It is in this context that we started our project which consists in realizing an embedded system for the elbow prosthesis functioning with the electromyographic (EMG) signal. Using a 3D printer, we printed a mechatronic device allowing us to reproduce in real-time both flexion and extension movements. The proposed classification model has proven to be very successful, allowing us to distinguish between flexion and extension movements with an accuracy of up to 86.2%. From these results, we generated a command signal to control the different motors of the prosthesis using an FPGA board to be able to offer a practical side to the forearm amputees.

articleTitle: Enhanced Vdc Bus Stability for PV and Battery Systems through an Optimized FOPID Controller using a Bidirectional DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In modern power systems, renewable energy sources (RES), such as wind turbine, photovoltaics and (BES) battery energy storage are becoming increasingly important. However, maintaining a stable direct voltage (Vdc) bus poses a challenge for these systems. This paper proposes an effective approach to improve Vdc bus stability by introducing an optimized Fractional-Order Proportional-Integral-Derivative (FOPID) controller, designed using a Genetic Algorithm (GA). Employing an FOPID strategy in the control of a bidirectional converter holds the potential to outperform an optimized PI (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller, particularly in terms of curtailing overshoot, bolstering stability.

articleTitle: Efficient RF Small-Signal Parasitic Parameters Extraction Technique For The Advanced MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Efficient modeling of advanced MOSFETS devices for microwave domain needs precise small-signal parasitic parameters extraction from S-parameters measurements. This article develops an efficient extraction technique to determine the values ​​of the equivalent circuit parasitic parameters of the advanced MOSFET. Using a linear regression technique, the proposed approach utilizes the transistor Z-matrix to extract the parasitic resistances and the Y-matrix to extract the parasitic capacitances at cold pinch-off conditions. The proposed approach was demonstrated by successful agreement between the simulation and the measurement over a broad frequency range.

articleTitle: Design of high-Performance Control Scheme for DFIG-Based Wind Energy Conversion System Supplies a MAS Using Hysteresis and the m & r Parameters Model
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel topology and control of wind energy conversion systems for Doubly Fed Induction Generator Asynchronous. A hysteresis current control is used to improve the de bus for rectifier and smart m and r control by model pulse-width modulation (PWM) of two-level supplies a load represents asynchronous machine. The advantages of this intelligent method such as fast dynamic answer and the easy implementation of nonlinearities and requires fewer calculations to choose the best switching state. Optimization of the m & r parameters of the PWM sin-triang inverter and a simulation is improved in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Comparison Steady of Single -Phase -Shift and Dual Phase- Shift - of Isolated Bidirectional Dual Active-Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: To evaluate the characteristic of isolated bidirectional Dual-Active-Bridge DC-DC (IBCD)modulation methods are proposed. Two different control strategy, single phase-shift control (SPS), dual-phase-shift control (DPS), are study and compared for a full-bridge-based isolated bidirectional dc-dc converter with detailed theoretical, analysis of operation mode and create mathematical models of transmission power, backflow power, and current stress. At last, simulation results findings attest to superior performance DPS control.

articleTitle: Electrical Discharges Influence on the Impedance/phase of Power Transformer Mineral Oil in the MegaHertzian Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Power transformers are critical components of the electrical power systems that are used for high voltage energy transmission and distribution. Insulating oil is required for their electrical insulation and cooling. Electrical discharges have the potential to degrade the insulation and alter the properties of the oil. This can lead to reduced transformer performance and a shorter lifespan. The present work will look at the effect of electrical discharges on the impedance of mineral oil in the frequency range of 20 Hz to 10 MHz. In this research investigation, we used a high-precision LCR meter to measure the impedance of Borak 22 new mineral oil, the commonly used insulating oil in Algerian power transformers. The measurements are made before and after a 50 series of electrical discharges in the frequency range of 20 Hz to 10 MHz with a point-plane electrode system and an electrode gap of 2.5 mm. Then, well correlations are found between the oil impedance and the discharges occurrence, especially in the 20 – 100 Hz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Intrusion Detection in IoT: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The rise of new complex attacks scenarios in Internet of things (IoT) environments necessitate more advanced and intelligent cyber defense techniques such as various Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) which are responsible for detecting and mitigating malicious activities in IoT networks without human intervention. To address this issue, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has been proposed in recent years, to automatically tackle intrusions/attacks. In this paper, a comprehensive survey of DRL-based IDS on IoT is presented. Furthermore, in this survey, the state-of-the-art DRL-based IDS methods have been classified into five categories including wireless sensor network (WSN), deep Q-network (QP), healthcare, hybrid, and other techniques. In addition, the most crucial performance metrics, namely accuracy, recall, precision, false negative rate (FNR), false positive rate (FPR), and F-measure, are detailed, in order to evaluate the performance of each proposed method. The paper provides a summary of datasets utilized in the studies as well.

articleTitle: Forest Fire Detection Using a Low Complex Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Forest fires have significant environmental and societal consequences, contributing to carbon emissions and endangering wildlife. Early detection of forest fires is crucial to reduce the extent of damage and improve firefighting efficiency. This research proposes a computer vision-based approach using a low complex Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for forest fire detection. The CNN architecture consists of three convolutional layers and a fully connected layer with only two neurons, offering a simple yet effective design. The proposed CNN achieves a good accuracy of 97.11% on the Deep Fire dataset, surpassing traditional machine learning and deep learning-based techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The low complexity of the model enables fast processing time, making it suitable for practical real-world applications.

articleTitle: Noise-Robust Speech Recognition: A Comparative Analysis of LSTM and CNN Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This paper proposes two techniques of automatic speech recognition (ASR) using deep-learning applied to the Aurora-2 dataset in mode clean and mode multi-condition on three test that has sort of noises: subway, restaurant, and suburban noises, denoted A, B, and C respectively. The proposed scheme has two ways of classification, the first approach employs convolution neural networks (CNN) which receive image representation of the speech (Spectrogram) as inputs, the second approach employs recurrent neural networks (RNN) with persistent short-term memory (LSTM) which receives Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs) as input features. A comparison has been conducted with a method that is based on the Hidden Markov models toolkit (HTK). Experiments shows that CNN provides better classification results than other methods in noisy environments, reaching an accuracy of 97.31% which is an improvement over the value of 90.93% and 96.31% compared to LSTM and HMM respectively in 20 dB, and accuracy of 42.28% which is an improvement over the value of 22.14% and 29.87% compared to LSTM and HMM in −5 dB.

articleTitle: Automatic Speech Recognition with BERT and CTC Transformers: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: This review paper provides a comprehensive analysis of recent advances in automatic speech recognition (ASR) with bidirectional encoder representations from transformers BERT and connectionist temporal classification (CTC) transformers. The paper first introduces the fundamental concepts of ASR and discusses the challenges associated with it. It then explains the architecture of BERT and CTC transformers and their potential applications in ASR. The paper reviews several studies that have used these models for speech recognition tasks and discusses the results obtained. Additionally, the paper highlights the limitations of these models and outlines potential areas for further research. All in all, this review provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners who are interested in ASR with BERT and CTC transformers.

articleTitle: Review of Transform Domain Medical Image Watermarking Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Nowadays, to enhance patient care and streamline the management of medical information, medical images obtained in hospitals or imaging centers can be readily shared among multiple healthcare professionals. However, this sharing often takes place over insecure networks, exposing medical images to various security threats where attackers aim to manipulate, steal, or destroy sensitive information, any variation to the medical record might result in an incorrect diagnosis and hence harm the patient's life. This highlights the increased need for security measures to ensure confidentiality, availability, and reliability, which encompass integrity and authenticity. Watermarking techniques have emerged as a popular and effective means of protecting patient data from these attacks and problems. Watermarking techniques exhibit a range of categorizations, encompassing factors such as their classification based on robustness, imperceptibility, capacity, and the transform domain. Transform domain watermarking techniques have garnered significant interest due to their ability to offer a high level of robustness against attacks, all while ensuring the imperceptibility of the watermark. In this review, we explore a variety of transform domain watermarking techniques specifically designed for medical images. Additionally, we provide a comparative analysis of different kinds of transform domains commonly employed in medical image watermarking.

articleTitle: Field Oriented Control with Improved PSO Algorithm for Open End Winding Induction Motor Fed by SVM Four Level Dual Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The field-oriented control (FOC) technique is implemented in order to improve the effectiveness and performance of variable speed control in Open-End Winding Induction Motor (OEWIM) drives. In recent studies, optimization techniques are being applied more and more to enhance control performance. The particle swarm optimization algorithm is the most popular technique. To enhance the speed response for OEWIM, the PSO method is utilized to find the optimal values of the proportional-integral (PI) controller's parameters for each speed, flux, and currents controller. This paper provides a novel approach based on the linearly decreasing inertia weight of the PSO algorithm that improves the variable speed control of FOC in OEWIM. In order to maintain a constant switching frequency, decreased harmonic distortion, and reduced common mode voltage (CMV), the FOC is combined with dual space vector modulation (SVM). In this context, a space vector modulation technique for a fourlevel inverter is suggested and implemented by supplying each end of an open-end stator winding induction motor with twolevel inverters. The advantages of the suggested control system have been confirmed using simulated results of various tests of the complete system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between a Deep Learning Model and a Region-Based Active Contour Model for Pulmonary Nodules Segmentation on CT
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of lung nodules on computed tomography (CT) scans plays a crucial role in assessing and managing suspected lung cancer patients. This study evaluates two approaches based on active contour and deep learning for pulmonary nodule segmentation on CT scans. The experiments were performed on a data set of 383 images from 111 patients with suspected lung nodules. The results showed that the method based on deep learning exceeded the conventional method of capturing complex patterns. The Jaccard and Dice coefficients obtained were 0.758 and 0.856, respectively, for the deep learning method, compared with 0.601 and 0.726 for the conventional method. A qualitative analysis of the segmentation results was conducted on juxta pleural, juxta-vascular, and well-circumscribed nodules to evaluate each approach's performance, strengths, and weaknesses in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Static Radio Transmission Power-Changing in Fog Computing: The Quick Energy-Draining Case Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Fog Computing has revolutionized edge computing by bringing computation and storage capabilities closer to the network edge. However, the energy constraints faced by mobile devices in fog computing environments pose significant challenges. Quick energy draining of mobile devices is particularly troublesome, impacting their usability and longevity. To address this issue, this paper proposes an innovative approach to adjust the transmission power of mobile devices in dense fog-enabled environments. By offering four power levels, we aim to prolong the battery lifespan of mobile devices while ensuring task offtoading capabilities to fog servers. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed transmission power adjustment mechanism. Lower transmission powers result in prolonged mobile device operation and slower energy consumption rates, positively impacting battery life. Mitigating the quick energy-draining problem in fog computing holds promising implications for sustainability and usability in resource-constrained environments. Further research and real-world implementations are needed for validation and optimization.

articleTitle: Optical Detection of UAVs Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Drone technologies advance has become the new weapon of choice for terror and criminal applications for civilian and military targets. Hence, it has opened for researchers a new challenging task as the safety and security of privacy, public and state entities. In the current manuscript, we propose a novel drone detection approach using deep Convolutional Neural Networks CNNs aims to provide a computer aided method defined as Visual Geometry Group 16 VGG 16 Model for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle UAVs identification and recognition using image processing that can effectively classify the drone and non-drone scenes, from the captured RGB based images. Features extraction is then applied using machine learning classifiers to enhance the accuracy of the detection systems. The drone's detection algorithm with deep CNNs has demonstrated the best performance for object detection with accuracy of 94.57%. Nevertheless, the experimental results show high reliability of the designed model to be validated and used for drone detection and recognition.

articleTitle: Towards the Exploration of dry Electrodes Performance in Bioimpedance Measurements based on The AD5933 Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Bioimpedance measurement plays a significant role in various diagnostic and therapeutic applications related to skin health and conditions, such as dermatological diagnostics, transdermal drug delivery, and wound healing. Additionally, it is important to obtain accurate bioelectrical signals, ensure contact stability, and maintain patient safety during electrical stimulation. For that, this study investigates the behavior of the electrode-skin impedance interaction for various types of electrodes gel and dry on four healthy subjects within the frequency range of 5 kHz to 50 kHz. The present study is explored using a low-cost bioimpedance measurement system design based on the AD5933 chip with a tetra-polar electrode configuration. The validation process consists on the comparison of the obtained bioimpedance measurements for the four subjects. Then, we've conducted further analysis by the measure of the mean and the standard deviation for each electrode's type. This comparative analysis allowed for a comprehensive assessment of the performance and consistency of the electrodes across the subjects. It also contributes to the understanding of electrode performance and the potential use of dry electrodes in bioimpedance measurements.

articleTitle: Reversible Fragile Watermarking for Medical Image Authentication in the Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Image authentication techniques play an important for a multitude of multimedia applications. When images are transmitted over insecure channels like the internet, they are susceptible to unauthorized alterations and manipulations. Therefore, it's important to protect images against these manipulations, particularly in sensitive domains like the medical field, where even a minor alteration can lead to critical diagnostic errors. In this paper, we present a reversible fragile watermarking technique for medical image authentication. The watermark is first generated from the cover image using the discrete cosine transform (DCT). The Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is then applied to the cover image, and the high-frequency sub-band (HH) is divided into 2 × 2 non-overlapping blocks. Afterward, the watermark is embedded into these blocks using a novel embedding technique. The experimental results demonstrate that the presented technique achieves a high watermarked image quality for both 8-bit and 16-bit images with a PSNR of 61.26 dB and 101.21 dB respectively. Furthermore, the presented method offers nearly perfect reversibility and remains highly sensitive to various attacks even malicious ones.

articleTitle: A Proposed Empirical Method of Weighing Matrices Determination in LQ Controller Applied
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: The LQ controller's simplicity sets it apart from numerous other controllers that necessitate complex calculations and expensive hardware. As a result, this controller has garnered significant attention in unmanned aerial vehicle research. Nevertheless, determining the weighting matrices Q and R for gain optimization poses a significant challenge for designers. This study presents a rapid assessment of Q and R matrices, employing the variances of navigation system measurements and the input magnitudes of the wireless guidance system. These evaluations ultimately yield a definitive gain matrix for implementation in an indoor mode mini quadrotor. Experimental testing further substantiates the efficacy of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: PSFB DC-DC LCLC Resonant Converter Voltage and Current Modes Control Using Arduino-Mega
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In this paper, the voltage and current modes control of phase shift full bridge (PSFB) DC-DC LCLC resonant converter implemented using Arduino-Mega board which will be intended to be employed as power supplies in arc welding GMAW (Gas Metal Arc Welding) or GTAW (Gas Tungsten Arc Welding) processes respectively, is presented. Firstly, the programmable phase shifting and dead time mechanisms are explained and fulfilled by suitable configuration of Timer/Counter units available on ATmega2560 microcontrollers-based Arduino-Mega board. Then, based on the reduced order averaged model (ROAM) of the converter, the PID controllers are designed. After, for experimentation and validation, the hardware in the loop (HIL) simulation using dSpace 1103 board in which the Arduino-Mega plays the role of the external hardware is tackled. Finally, the HIL simulation results confirm the effectiveness of ROAM based PID controller design which show fairly good performances despite the load variation and DC supply voltage disturbances on the one hand, and on the other hand they justify the exploitation of Arduino-Mega board which belongs to open-source hardware and software products in arc welding power supplies (AWPS) control.

articleTitle: An adaptive gains sliding mode controller applied to wind turbine benchmark model under different faults
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Electricity generated from wind energy is increasing day by day globally; which requires us to give importance to the reliability of wind turbines so that the wind turbines continue to produce energy and keep the possibility of extracting the maximum power from the wind while ensuring the necessary operating performance, The work performed in this paper presents an adaptive gain sliding mode controller applied to wind turbine benchmark model. This work aims to investigate the effect of such a controller under a different scenario of sensors fault working in a full load zone. Moreover, a comparison analysis between the adaptive gain sliding mode controller and the proportional integral in terms of fault tolerance is presented. The proposed control approach for the variable-speed wind turbines is presented using a wind turbine Benchmark model of a three-blade horizontal axis variable speed with a nominal power of 4.8 MW.

articleTitle: Adversarial Example Detection Techniques in Speech Recognition Systems: A review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is a crucial application of deep learning in today's world. However, ASR systems are vulnerable to attacks from malicious actors who can create adversarial examples to fool the system into producing incorrect outputs. Adversarial example detection techniques are being developed to mitigate the risk of such attacks. This review analyzes the effectiveness of various adversarial example detection techniques in the context of ASR systems. It begins by explaining the concept of adversarial examples and their potential impact on ASR systems as well as the most used evaluation metrics. Then, it provides an overview of the different types of adversarial attacks that can be launched against ASR systems. Upon reading this review, researchers are able to identify the existing weakness in ASR, and evade them in their future proposed schemes.

articleTitle: Applications of Deep Reinforcement Learning in Wireless Networks-A Recent Review
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques have gained substantial attention in recent years for future wireless networks. They can overcome the ever-increasing challenges of wireless environment and limitations of traditional techniques. Some applications of DRL for future wireless and mobile networks are network optimization, network control, power management, mobile edge computation (MEC), offloading, edge cachings, network slicing and many others. This paper mainly addresses network optimization specifically energy optimization, and secondly resource allocation. A recent literature review is presented by looking at research so far achieved, DRL methods used, and future research directions.

articleTitle: State of the Art of Brain MRI Tissue Segmentation Techniques and Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Analysis of medical brain images for brain components identification and detection has become a formidable challenge in the field of medical applications, which not only help guide or monitor medical interventions, but also to ensure their accuracy and the success level of medical treatment once the cerebral abnormalities were identified and localized. Medical brain images analysis and synthesis are mainly based on the process of image segmentation technique, this process, consists of dividing an image into two or more homogeneous regions based on common characteristics such as intensity, color, texture, etc. This article presents the state of the art for MRI brain components segmentation techniques and discusses the different segmentation techniques and methods used in medical images analyses, and more precisely for medical brain images to detect and select brain components, these methods and techniques are categorized into five categories according to various criteria, including the image treatment process and the nature level (prior knowledge) employed on the proposed methodologies and methods. Finally, we are shedding light on the strengths and limitations for each segmentation technique to serves as a valuable resource into the field of medical brain image segmentation and analysis techniques for researchers to contribute and develop new segmentation techniques and methods more accurate.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Automated Detection and Classification of Dysarthria Severity
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Dysarthria, a speech disorder caused by neuro-motor problems resulting in impaired articulation, requires an assessment of its severity for diagnostic and monitoring purposes. Additionally, accurate severity classification facilitates the development of automated dysarthric speech detection and classification systems. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into detecting dysarthric voices within a collection of normal voice samples, followed by the dysarthria severity classification utilizing neural network frameworks, specifically long short-term memory network (LSTM) and recurrent neural network (RNN). The study employs various features including Mel frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), formants, prosodic parameters, and voice quality. The performance of these models is evaluated against a baseline support vector machine (SVM) classifier using the Nemours corpus database. Remarkably, the highest classification accuracy achieved for this corpus is 99.69%. Detailed analysis demonstrates that selecting an appropriate neural network architecture yields superior performance compared to the conventional SVM classifier.

articleTitle: Support Vector Regression for Predicting Intra-day Photovoltaic Generation in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: In this study, we conducted an experimental assessment to predict intra-day values of a grid-connected photovoltaic power plant positioned within the Djelfa province, specifically in the Ain El Ibel commune of Algeria. The Support Vector Machine Regression is used. The experiments consist of investigating the best kernel function that fits accurately the processed data, in addition to the impact of the historical input layer length. Thus, the Polynomial kernel function, the Radial Basis Function, and the linear kernel function were individually tested. The results show that the Radial Bias function gives better results using a few historical inputs. However, when the historical input data becomes larger, the polynomial kernel function competes with the RBF. Despite this, the calculated mean average of the performance parameters reveals that the Radial Basis function gives slightly better statistical metrics (r = 0.8938, MAE =0.0690, RMSE = 0.0.0947, rRMSE=0.2635, NRMSE=0.0961) compared with the polynomial (r = 0.8886, MAE = 0.0702, RMSE = 0.0991, rRMSE=0.2748, NRMSE=0.0972). In this study, the linear kernel shows the weakest parameters (r = 0.8329, MAE =0.0918, RMSE = 0.1192, rRMSE = 0.3267, NRMSE = 0.1204).

articleTitle: Word from the Chairs
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy and Measurement (IC2EM)
abstract: Nestled in the vibrant heart of Medea, Algeria, ICEM'2023 transcended the conventional boundaries of a mere conference; it became a crucible where the destiny of electronics, energy, and measurement took form. From November 28th to 30th, 2023, this intellectual melting pot pulsed with groundbreaking research, spirited discussions, and collaborations that ignited a chain reaction of innovation.
